dialogues.title: Знакомство (Getting Acquainted)
dialogues.scene: Two people meet and introduce themselves at a cultural event.

lines.speaker: Анна
lines.ref: Hello! My name is Anna.

lines.speaker: Иван
lines.ref: Nice to meet you. I'm Ivan.

lines.speaker: Анна
lines.ref: Where are you from, Ivan?

lines.speaker: Иван
lines.ref: I'm from Saint Petersburg. And you?

lines.speaker: Анна
lines.target: Я живу в Москве. Кем вы работаете?
lines.ref: I live in Moscow. What do you do for work?

lines.speaker: Иван
lines.ref: I work as an engineer. And you?

lines.speaker: Анна
lines.ref: I'm a teacher. I teach English.

lines.speaker: Иван
lines.ref: How interesting! Glad to meet you.

lines.speaker: Анна
lines.ref: Likewise. See you!

dialogues.note: When stating a profession with работать, the job goes in the instrumental case: работаю инженером, not 'инженер'. Russians also often use the polite вы with people they've just met.

dialogues.title: В кафе (At the Café)
dialogues.scene: A customer orders tea, coffee and a dish, then asks for the bill.

lines.speaker: Официант
lines.ref: Good afternoon! What would you like to order?

lines.speaker: Гость
lines.target: Здравствуйте. Один чай с лимоном, пожалуйста.
lines.ref: Hello. One tea with lemon, please.

lines.speaker: Официант
lines.ref: Anything else?

lines.speaker: Гость
lines.target: Да, я хочу борщ и чёрный кофе.
lines.ref: Yes, I'd like borscht and a black coffee.

lines.speaker: Официант
lines.ref: Coffee with sugar?

lines.speaker: Гость
lines.ref: No, without sugar, thank you.

lines.speaker: Официант
lines.ref: All right, one minute.

lines.speaker: Гость
lines.target: Всё было очень вкусно. Счёт, пожалуйста.
lines.ref: Everything was very tasty. The bill, please.

lines.speaker: Официант
lines.ref: Of course. That'll be five hundred rubles.

lines.speaker: Гость
lines.ref: Here you go. Thank you!

dialogues.note: In a café the phrase С вас... literally means 'from you [is due]...' and is the standard way staff state the amount owed. Borscht (борщ) is a beet soup served hot or cold.

dialogues.title: Как пройти? (Asking Directions)
dialogues.scene: A tourist in Moscow asks how to reach Red Square, the metro and a pharmacy.

lines.speaker: Турист
lines.target: Извините, как пройти к Красной площади?
lines.ref: Excuse me, how do I get to Red Square?

lines.speaker: Прохожий
lines.target: Идите прямо, а потом поверните налево.
lines.ref: Go straight, and then turn left.

lines.speaker: Турист
lines.ref: Is it far?

lines.speaker: Прохожий
lines.ref: No, about ten minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: Турист
lines.ref: And where is the nearest metro station?

lines.speaker: Прохожий
lines.ref: The metro is over there, around the corner.

lines.speaker: Турист
lines.ref: Thank you! I also need a pharmacy.

lines.speaker: Прохожий
lines.ref: The pharmacy is located opposite the bank.

lines.speaker: Турист
lines.ref: Thank you very much for your help!

lines.speaker: Прохожий
lines.ref: Don't mention it. All the best!

dialogues.note: Russians commonly give walking time as 'минут десять' with the number AFTER the noun to signal 'about ten minutes'. Reversing the order (десять минут) means exactly ten.

dialogues.title: В супермаркете (At the Supermarket)
dialogues.scene: A shopper asks where items are, buys quantities and pays at the cashier.

lines.speaker: Покупатель
lines.target: Извините, где я могу найти хлеб?
lines.ref: Excuse me, where can I find bread?

lines.speaker: Сотрудник
lines.ref: Bread is in the third aisle, on the right.

lines.speaker: Покупатель
lines.ref: And do you have milk?

lines.speaker: Сотрудник
lines.target: Да, молоко в холодильнике у входа.
lines.ref: Yes, milk is in the fridge by the entrance.

lines.speaker: Покупатель
lines.ref: Please give me two kilograms of apples.

lines.speaker: Сотрудник
lines.ref: Here you are. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Покупатель
lines.ref: No, that's all. Where is the checkout?

lines.speaker: Сотрудник
lines.ref: The checkout is over there, by the exit.

lines.speaker: Кассир
lines.target: С вас триста рублей. Вам пакет нужен?
lines.ref: That's three hundred rubles. Do you need a bag?

lines.speaker: Покупатель
lines.ref: Yes, and I'm paying by card.

vocab: в третьем ряду (in the third aisle)
dialogues.note: After 2, 3, 4 the counted noun takes the genitive singular (два килограмма), but with яблок the fruit itself is genitive plural because a weight quantity governs it. Paying 'by card' uses the instrumental: картой.

dialogues.title: В кассе вокзала (Buying a Train Ticket)
dialogues.scene: A traveler books a train ticket: destination, class, date, and one-way or return.

lines.speaker: Пассажир
lines.target: Здравствуйте, мне нужен билет до Казани.
lines.ref: Hello, I need a ticket to Kazan.

lines.speaker: Кассир
lines.ref: For what date?

lines.speaker: Пассажир
lines.ref: For September fifteenth, if possible.

lines.speaker: Кассир
lines.target: В один конец или туда и обратно?
lines.ref: One-way or round trip?

lines.speaker: Пассажир
lines.target: Туда и обратно. И желательно нижнюю полку.
lines.ref: Round trip. And preferably a lower berth.

lines.speaker: Кассир
lines.ref: Compartment or open-plan carriage?

lines.speaker: Пассажир
lines.ref: A compartment, please. What time is departure?

lines.speaker: Кассир
lines.target: Поезд отправляется в двадцать два часа десять минут.
lines.ref: The train departs at 22:10.

lines.speaker: Пассажир
lines.ref: Great. How much does that cost?

lines.speaker: Кассир
lines.target: Четыре тысячи рублей. Ваш паспорт, пожалуйста.
lines.ref: Four thousand rubles. Your passport, please.

lines.speaker: Пассажир
lines.ref: Here it is. Thank you very much!

dialogues.note: Russian long-distance trains distinguish купе (four-berth closed compartment) from плацкарт (open bunk carriage). Ticket purchases require a passport, and the 24-hour clock is standard for timetables.

dialogues.title: На почте (At the Post Office)
dialogues.scene: A customer sends a parcel, buys stamps and asks about delivery time and cost.

lines.speaker: Клиент
lines.target: Добрый день! Я хочу отправить посылку в Германию.
lines.ref: Good afternoon! I want to send a parcel to Germany.

lines.speaker: Оператор
lines.ref: What's inside? Please fill out the form.

lines.speaker: Клиент
lines.ref: There are books and a small gift inside.

lines.speaker: Оператор
lines.ref: Put the parcel on the scale.

lines.speaker: Клиент
lines.ref: How much will delivery cost?

lines.speaker: Оператор
lines.ref: Eight hundred rubles by regular mail.

lines.speaker: Клиент
lines.ref: And how long does the parcel take?

lines.speaker: Оператор
lines.ref: Approximately two weeks.

lines.speaker: Клиент
lines.target: Хорошо. Ещё мне нужны пять марок.
lines.ref: All right. I also need five stamps.

lines.speaker: Оператор
lines.target: Пожалуйста. С вас всего девятьсот рублей.
lines.ref: Here you go. That's nine hundred rubles in total.

lines.speaker: Клиент
lines.ref: Thanks for your help. All the best!

vocab: заполнить бланк (to fill out a form)
как долго идёт (how long it takes)
dialogues.note: For mail 'in transit' Russians use the motion verb идти — посылка идёт две недели literally means 'the parcel goes for two weeks'. After the number пять, марок takes the genitive plural.
